title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet

epigraph.quote: Net profit is an opinion shaped by capitalization policies; free cash flow after all capitalized development is the only verdict that cannot be argued with.
epigraph.author: Institutional Field Notes

web_blocks.html: A ten-year audit from FY19 through H1 FY27 exposes a wide gap between reported sales growth and economic value creation [1][2]. Consolidated sales grew from ₹63 Cr in FY19 (dipping to ₹42 Cr in FY21) to ₹132.90 Cr in FY26 and ₹144 Cr TTM [1][2]. Yet net profit never broke out. PAT stood at ₹7 Cr in FY19, ₹5 Cr in FY22, ₹3 Cr in FY24, ₹1 Cr in FY25, and ₹5.33 Cr in FY26 [1][2]. Over that eight-year span, cumulative Free Cash Flow was deeply negative at roughly −₹46 Cr [1]. Meanwhile, ROE languished at 2.77%, with ROCE at 6.31% [1].

Three forensic mechanisms explain this chronic profit-and-cash squeeze. First is aggressive Ind AS 38 capitalization of internal software [2][6]. Statutory auditors (P G Bhagwat LLP) flag Intangible Assets Under Development (IAUD) as a Key Audit Matter [6]. Management uses wide judgment to decide how much developer payroll to capitalize instead of expensing [6]. At March 31, 2026, Other Intangible Assets stood at ₹70.65 Cr and IAUD at ₹19.56 Cr [2]. Combined intangibles reached ₹90.22 Cr, or 35.6% of total assets (₹253.54 Cr) and 52.5% of owners' equity (₹171.76 Cr) [2]. By September 30, 2026, Fixed/Intangible Assets jumped from ₹81 Cr to ₹111 Cr as ₹20 Cr of IAUD moved into active use [1]. Quarterly Depreciation & Amortization thus climbed from ₹3.41 Cr (Sep 2023) to ₹5.86 Cr (Mar 2026) and ₹6.85 Cr in Q2 FY27 [1].

web_blocks.html: Second is working-capital quality and credit losses. Billed trade receivables fell from ₹43.58 Cr (FY25) to ₹34.63 Cr (FY26) [2]. Yet unbilled Contract Assets rose to ₹53.52 Cr (₹52.79 Cr current plus ₹0.73 Cr non-current) [2]. SoftTech also booked ₹12.08 Cr in doubtful-debt provisions and write-offs in FY26 [2]. That charge equals 9.1% of annual sales and 2.3x consolidated net profit [2]. Third is balance-sheet leverage and ownership dilution. At March 31, 2026, total debt was ₹31.74 Cr (₹28.27 Cr current plus ₹3.47 Cr non-current), alongside ₹7.10 Cr of lease liabilities [2]. Screener reports ₹39 Cr in combined borrowings and leases, with CARE A3 on short-term facilities [1][19]. Cash and bank balances totaled ₹32.91 Cr (₹12.71 Cr cash plus ₹20.20 Cr other bank balances), aided by prior equity raises [2]. Still, repeated dilution cut promoter holding from 32.05% in March 2024 to 18.89% by September 2026 [1].

The multi-year ratio trend shows why return on capital remains the key bottleneck [1][2]. Consolidated ROCE fell from 13% (FY20) to 7% (FY21), 8% (FY22–FY23), 6% (FY24), 4% (FY25), and 6.31% (FY26) [1]. Three-year average ROE hovered at 2.06%, with FY26 ROE at 2.77% [1]. Screener's Working Capital Days fell from 406 days (FY21) to 79.3 days (FY26) [1]. That drop came as Days Payable stretched to 259–450 days and billed Debtor Days fell to 95 [1]. Even so, capital employed kept swelling as ₹30–34 Cr/year went into Fixed/Intangible Assets and IAUD [1][2]. Over FY19–FY26, cumulative cash flow from operations never once covered annual capex and intangibles additions [1][2]. That eight-year streak proves negative FCF is structural, not a one-quarter blip. Unless asset turns on the ₹111 Cr fixed base rise sharply or capitalization slows, ROE will stay below cost of capital.

web_blocks.title: The Forensic Bottom Line
paragraphs: SoftTech is not an accounting fiction. It owns real municipal deployments, ₹132.90 Cr of audited sales, and ₹32.91 Cr of cash and bank balances [2].

Still, it must stop capitalizing ₹30+ Cr/year of development costs and shrink its ₹53.52 Cr unbilled asset pile without ₹12 Cr write-offs. Until it earns well above a 2.77% ROE, it fails the test of a quality compounder.

book_paragraphs: If Chapter 3 showed you the single-year ₹100 waterfall, Chapter 6 zooms out to the full eight-year movie. And the picture is unmistakable. Between FY19 and FY26, SoftTech Engineers grew its annual revenue from ₹63 Cr to ₹132.90 Cr. Yet over those exact same eight years, Free Cash Flow was negative every single year: −₹2 Cr, −₹13 Cr, −₹6 Cr, −₹5 Cr, −₹9 Cr, −₹3 Cr, −₹7 Cr, and −₹1.31 Cr.

Pause and let that sink in. Not once in eight years did the business generate enough operating cash to cover its own software development and capital expenditure. Every rupee of equity growth on the balance sheet, Reserves rising from ₹51 Cr in FY19 to ₹158 Cr in FY26, came from issuing new shares and warrants to outside investors, not from retained free cash flow.

Look at why the auditors, P G Bhagwat LLP, highlight 'Intangible Assets Under Development' as a Key Audit Matter. By March 2026, SoftTech had ₹70.65 Cr of intangible assets and ₹19.56 Cr of IAUD on its books, ₹90.22 Cr in total, more than half of its entire shareholders' equity! And in H1 FY27, another ₹20 Cr moved from development into active assets, pushing quarterly amortization to ₹6.85 Cr.

When you combine ₹90.22 Cr of capitalized intangibles, ₹53.52 Cr of unbilled contract assets, ₹12.08 Cr of FY26 bad-debt write-offs, a 2.77% ROE, and a promoter stake that fell 21.6 percentage points to 18.89%, you and I have our answer on business quality, long before we ever look at a stock chart or a share price.

Let's look at the 10-year ratios table together, because one number tells the whole story: ROCE. Back in FY20, SoftTech earned a 13% return on capital employed. By FY21 it fell to 7%, then 8% in FY22 and FY23, 6% in FY24, 4% in FY25, and 6.31% in FY26. Meanwhile, ROE sits at 2.77%.

Why did ROCE fall in half even as revenue more than doubled from FY20's ₹58 Cr to FY26's ₹133 Cr? Because Capital Employed grew even faster than operating profit! Equity Capital plus Reserves swelled from ₹66 Cr in FY20 to ₹172 Cr in FY26 via repeated share issuances, and almost all of that capital got locked up in ₹90.22 Cr of capitalized intangibles and ₹53.52 Cr of unbilled contract assets.

When you also notice that Days Payable stretched to 259 days in FY26 (and 450 days in FY25), you realize that even the improvement in headline Working Capital Days from 406 days to 79 days came partly from stretching trade payables and writing off ₹12.08 Cr of bad debts, not from effortless cash velocity.

Chapter 6 is where every comforting story gets tested against ten years of audited numbers. Pull up the Screener consolidated profit-and-loss, balance-sheet, and cash-flow tables alongside the FY26 audited results, and trace the trajectory from FY19 through TTM FY27. Sales have more than doubled from ₹63 Cr in FY19 to ₹133 Cr in FY26 (and ₹144 Cr TTM). Operating profit has grown from ₹16 Cr to ₹33 Cr. On an EBITDA-only screen, SoftTech looks like a steady compounder.

Now look one layer deeper at what happens below EBITDA. In FY19, depreciation was ₹5 Cr. By FY26, it reached ₹22.83 Cr. And in Q2 FY27 alone, it hit ₹6.85 Cr, an annualized run rate of ₹27.4 Cr. Why? Because under Ind AS 38, SoftTech has been capitalizing ₹30+ Cr a year of internal software development onto its balance sheet. Total Intangibles plus Intangible Assets Under Development (IAUD) now stand at ₹90.22 Cr, 52.5% of total shareholders' equity of ₹171.8 Cr.

Next, check the working-capital ledger. Headline Screener ratios celebrate that Debtor Days fell from 158 to 95.1 days (₹34.63 Cr). But read Note 9 of the audited balance sheet: sitting right next to billed trade receivables is ₹53.52 Cr of Contract Assets (unbilled revenue). Add them together and SoftTech is carrying ₹88.15 Cr, 66.3% of an entire year's revenue, or 242 days, waiting to be billed and collected from municipal and PSU clients. Meanwhile, FY26 doubtful-debt provisions jumped 4.3x to ₹12.08 Cr. That combination, rising amortization, unbilled government receivables, and eight straight years of negative FCF, is why we rated KPI health as FAIL before ever looking at the stock price.

book_callouts.title: The Price-Blind Verdict Before Valuation
book_callouts.text: This is why we do Pass 1 completely blind to stock price. Knowing only the business, the unit economics, and the cash-flow forensics, we can already classify SoftTech as a cyclical, capital-hungry GovTech hybrid with serious accounting and governance watch-items—not a quality compounder.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Four Financial Statements Together
paragraphs: Look at the four snapshot tables side by side. On the P&L, you see exciting 40% sales growth in FY26. On the Cash Flow statement, you see ₹31 Cr of CFO. An investor who stops there thinks they have found a hidden SaaS gem.

But the moment you connect the Balance Sheet to the Investing Cash Flow, the illusion breaks: ₹30.50 Cr of cash walked right back out the door into intangibles development, ₹53.52 Cr of revenue sat unbilled in Contract Assets, and ₹12.08 Cr of prior receivables had to be written off or provided. That is why ROE sits at 2.77% and ROCE at 6.31%.

callouts.title: What Pass 2 Must Answer
callouts.text: Now that we know the exact forensic reality of SoftTech's business quality, Pass 2 will test whether the market price already discounts these flaws—or whether investors are paying a SaaS multiple for a negative-FCF GovTech contractor.

book_subsections.title: Why We Stop Here Before Looking at Any Price
paragraphs: You and I have now completed a full, price-blind forensic audit of SoftTech Engineers, without once glancing at a stock chart, a share price, or a P/E multiple. That discipline is priceless, because it prevents market momentum from seducing us into ignoring 2.77% ROE, eight years of negative free cash flow, ₹90.22 Cr of capitalized intangibles, and an 18.89% promoter stake.

In Pass 2, we will finally reveal the market price, run a reverse DCF, check the Stage 2 technical structure, and weigh both sides of the aisle. Whatever the market is charging for SoftTech today, we now know the exact quality of the business behind the ticker.

callouts.title: Pass 1 Forensic Summary
callouts.text: Real Indian GovTech niche (AutoDCR/CivitPERMIT) + ₹302 Cr order book, offset by 8-year negative FCF, ₹90.22 Cr capitalized intangibles, ₹53.52 Cr unbilled contract assets, ₹12.08 Cr FY26 bad-debt write-off, 2.77% ROE, and 18.89% promoter holding.

book_subsections.title: Summary of the Ten-Year Forensic Ledger
paragraphs: Stepping back from the line-by-line tables, the ten-year forensic verdict on SoftTech Engineers is crystal clear. From FY19 to FY26, cumulative cash flow from operations was positive, yet cumulative capital expenditure, driven overwhelmingly by ₹150+ Cr of capitalized software development and IAUD, exceeded CFO in every single year. Eight consecutive years of negative free cash flow is not a one-quarter timing quirk; it is the structural signature of the current operating model.

Combined with a 2.77% ROE, a 6.31% ROCE, ₹90.22 Cr of balance-sheet intangibles (52.5% of net worth), and ₹88.15 Cr tied up in billed receivables plus unbilled contract assets, SoftTech has not yet demonstrated that it can compound owners' capital above its cost of equity. That is the exact price-blind foundation we carry into our valuation and technical audit.
